## __WINDOW_MD__ -- __MEASURETYPE_MD__ (Between Subjects)

Single condition ("__BIN1_MD__"), compared between the between-subjects groups.

```{r}
#| label: __CHUNKLABEL__
#| results: asis
grp <- dat %>% filter(measure_type == "__MEASURETYPE_R__", window == "__WINDOW_R__", bin == "__BIN1_R__") %>% droplevels()
__BLOCKMATCHDIAGNOSTIC__
grp <- per_person(grp)

descr_list <- list()
res2_list <- list()
anova_list <- list()
pw_list <- list()
for (ch in unique(grp$channel)) {
  tryCatch({
  d <- grp %>% filter(channel == ch, !is.na(value)) %>% droplevels()
  n_groups <- n_distinct(d$group)
  if (n_groups < 2 || nrow(d) < 2) {
    res2_list[[ch]] <- tibble(Channel = ch, Test = NA_character_,
      Note = "Skipped: fewer than two groups have a usable value for this channel.")
    next
  }
  tag <- str_replace_all(paste("__WINDOW_R__", "__MEASURETYPE_R__", ch, sep = "_"), "[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_")

  descr_list[[ch]] <- d %>% group_by(group) %>% summarise(M = mean(value), SD = sd(value), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(channel = ch, .before = 1)

  if (n_groups == 2) {
    # The test of record and its check, both, always (see paired-section.qmd). The
    # Shapiro-Wilk p is of the values about their own group's mean: the raw values
    # of two groups pooled are bimodal exactly when the groups differ, and were
    # choosing the rank test for 77% of samples at d = 4.
    lv <- levels(droplevels(factor(d$group)))
    tt <- t.test(value ~ group, data = d)
    eff <- cohens_d_ci(d$value[d$group == lv[1]], d$value[d$group == lv[2]])
    bf <- bf10_ttest(formula = value ~ group,
                     data = as.data.frame(d %>% mutate(group = droplevels(factor(group)))))
    res2 <- tibble(Channel = ch, Test = "Welch two-sample t-test", Statistic = unname(tt$statistic), df = apa_num(unname(tt$parameter), 1),
                   p = apa_p(tt$p.value), Effect = "Cohen's d", Estimate = eff$effsize,
                   CI_low = eff$conf.low, CI_high = eff$conf.high,
                   BF10 = fmt_bf(bf), Evidence = bf_word(bf),
                   Shapiro_Wilk_p = shapiro_note(d$value - ave(d$value, d$group)))
    p_grp <- tt$p.value
    omnibus <- bind_rows(omnibus, tibble(group = tag, window = "__WINDOW_R__", measure = "__MEASURETYPE_R__", channel = ch, contrast = NA_character_, role = "primary", design = "indep_t", test = "welch_t_test", p = p_grp,
                                          estimate = eff$effsize, conf.low = eff$conf.low, conf.high = eff$conf.high))
    wt <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(value ~ group, data = d, conf.int = TRUE)), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(wt)) {
      rb <- rank_biserial_ci(value ~ group, data = d)
      res2 <- bind_rows(res2, tibble(Channel = ch, Test = "Mann-Whitney U", Statistic = unname(wt$statistic), df = "--",
                                     p = apa_p(wt$p.value), Effect = "Rank-biserial r", Estimate = rb$effsize,
                                     CI_low = rb$conf.low, CI_high = rb$conf.high))
    }
    res2_list[[ch]] <- res2
  } else {
    # Welch's one-way ANOVA, not the classic (Fisher) one -- it does not
    # assume equal variances across groups, which is routinely violated
    # and rarely checked; matches the 2-group branch above already using
    # Welch's t-test rather than Student's for the same reason (Delacre
    # et al., 2019). Games-Howell is its matching post-hoc, for the same
    # reason Tukey (which assumes equal variances/group sizes) is not used.
    aov <- tryCatch(welch_anova_test(data = d, formula = value ~ group), error = function(e) NULL)
    p_grp <- NA_real_
    if (!is.null(aov)) {
      p_grp <- aov$p[1]
      anova_list[[ch]] <- as.data.frame(aov) %>% mutate(channel = ch, .before = 1)
    }
    pw_list[[ch]] <- (d %>% games_howell_test(value ~ group)) %>% mutate(channel = ch, .before = 1)

    omnibus <- bind_rows(omnibus, tibble(group = tag, window = "__WINDOW_R__", measure = "__MEASURETYPE_R__", channel = ch, contrast = NA_character_, role = "primary", design = "welch_anova", test = "omnibus", p = p_grp,
                                          estimate = NA_real_, conf.low = NA_real_, conf.high = NA_real_))
  }
  }, error = function(e) {
    res2_list[[ch]] <<- tibble(Channel = ch, Test = NA_character_, Note = sprintf("Could not be analysed: %s", conditionMessage(e)))
  })
}

descr_all <- bind_rows(descr_list)
if (nrow(descr_all) > 0) {
  cat(as_raw_html(apa_gt(descr_all, "Descriptive Statistics by Channel")))
}

common_layers <- list(
  geom_jitter(width = 0.06, alpha = 0.6),
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 3),
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", width = 0.1),
  labs(x = "Group", y = "__YLABEL__"),
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2"),
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2"),
  facet_wrap(~channel),
  alz_theme(),
  theme(legend.position = "none")
)
p <- ggplot(grp %>% filter(!is.na(value)), aes(group, value, colour = group, fill = group)) + violin_layers() + common_layers
print(p)

res2_all <- bind_rows(res2_list)
if (nrow(res2_all) > 0) {
  cat(as_raw_html(blank_missing(apa_gt(res2_all, "Test Result by Channel"))))
  tests_used <- unique(na.omit(res2_all$Test))
